start.text: # Audio Recording (English Translation)
1Q. Office Suite –
Hospital, Third Floor

It shouldn't take them long to discover that the shaking opened a passage in the rear of the southern alcove, which is now the only means they have to get out of the crypt. The tunnel is only about two and a half feet wide, and immediately descends in stair-like steps. The passage turns slightly back and forth, so it's impossible to tell how far it goes. If they test for air flow using a flame, there definitely seems to be a draft leading into that passage.
A Few Pointers on Running Viral from Bud

attached_note_selectors.text: Note that most of these aren't true, or are mingled with half-truths. When hearing a rumor, the Keeper should have the investigators make an Intelligence check to see it for the nonsense it is.

The rowboat is in rough shape, though it should hold together for a single trip back to Perla on the mainland with all five of the Krew onboard (especially given Enoch's size). Anyone attempting to row the boat should make a STR check against the following chart:
Note: Unless otherwise indicated, each of the above options requires a Sanity check (0/1).

selector.text: While the grenades do damage Hastalÿk, they are not enough to stop it entirely. Each has the chance of delaying its progress by one to four rounds depending on how successful they are at throwing. Keepers are recommended to give any investigator with a Dexterity of 60 or higher a Bonus Die on their throw. Alternately, the Keeper may opt to simply have them make a Dexterity check since they are throwing at such a big target with a weapon that affects a large area.

required_literal_substrings: \*Delivers 4D10 damage to those within 3 yards, 2D10 to those within 6 yards and 1D10 to those within 9 yards. Continues to inflict 2D10 fire damage for 3 rounds.

attached_note_selectors.text: While the grenades do damage Hastalÿk, they are not enough to stop it entirely. Each has the chance of delaying its progress by one to four rounds depending on how successful they are at throwing. Keepers are recommended to give any investigator with a Dexterity of 60 or higher a Bonus Die on their throw. Alternately, the Keeper may opt to simply have them make a Dexterity check since they are throwing at such a big target with a weapon that affects a large area.

If the throw is fumbled, the grenade is dropped. The Keeper can give the investigator the opportunity to find and throw the grenade far enough to avoid damage or they can simply run. The former will require a Hard Dexterity check, or suffer 4D10 points of damage. The latter requires a Strength check, with the result determining the damage (if any). Failure means suffering 4D10 damage, while a Regular success means 2d10 damage. A Hard success reduces the damage to 1D10, and an Extreme success means avoiding all damage.
Note that these attacks are cumulative, so that if two investigators manage to land grenades within 6 yards, The Devourer would be delayed for a total of 4 rounds.

These encounters are guidelines for the Keeper, and don't represent all possible phenomena. They can be rolled randomly (D12) or selected based on the Investigator or situation. The Keeper should have milder encounters earlier during the investigation, and slowly escalate things as the night progresses. Each encounter has a suggestion for Sanity loss, but even these should be adjusted based on the intensity of the event and the specific situation. Early encounters aren't likely to trigger a Sanity check, while later encounters will almost certainly have some sort of impact on the Investigators' Sanity.

At first, everything will seem like the typical haunting investigation that the Investigators have experienced a hundred times before. By turning up the creepiness slowly, they won't necessarily notice when they make the transition to something that is genuinely supernatural. When describing any of these encounters, the Keeper should try to leave room for some sort of rational explanation. For example, if they see a light through the trees, they may go to investigate and notice that some of the lights from the mainland are visible. This gives them a plausible explanation that should make them comfortable enough to keep investigating.

Remember that the goal is to lure the Investigators into the crypt at midnight for the witch board session. If an encounter really seems to rattle an Investigator, maybe one of the viewers offers \$500 for them to continue. It's surprising what a little hard cash can do to justify a risk.

start_selector.text: 2 Cold Spot – It may just feel a little cooler early in the investigation, but as things become more 'real' they could see their breath and have frost form on smooth surfaces like metal and glass. [Sanity Loss (0/1)]

10 Dead Birds – A room with the floor littered with the corpses of birds of all regional types. They all have a black ooze coming out of their eyes and mouth similar to that found on the half submerged rowboat and in the rickety dock. [Sanity Loss (0/1)]

attached_note_selectors.text: Due to the corrupt nature of this location, the Sanity rules have been slightly modified to reflect this. When an Investigator experiences a Bout of Madness, they automatically gain 1 level of Taint and the Keeper should have the player roll a D10 on the following chart. Note that only the Investigator suffering the Bout of Madness sees any of this, and when the episode ends (after 1D10 rounds), there is no sign of whatever they experienced.

These are some possible examples of the kind of paranormal phenomena that the Spektral Krew could encounter while exploring the island and hospital. This isn't intended to be an exhaustive list, and the Keeper should feel free to roll on it as is, or use it for inspiration for their own phenomena. The idea is to provide paranormal experiences to keep them interested, while making them ambiguous enough to be dismissed with more naturalistic explanations by those who prefer not to believe in such things.

xrefs.source_line: He is an absolute bear of a man who was hired by Marco as a bodyguard and investigator, just in case they ever get into danger with people as opposed to the supernatural, as despite being quite a kind soul, he is physically very intimidating. Enoch has a broad smile and an infectious laugh. He's actually a lot smarter than he looks and a competent investigator who picks up on things the others don't. Enoch doesn't fully understand it, but he actually has The Sight (see Appendix), though he puts a lot of what he sees down to just indulging in too much drink and drugs.

segments.source_text: Taint level of 10 (see p.62 for details)

xrefs.source_line: Em learned about the Krew investigating the island around a week ago from an anonymous tipoff – this was actually by Maya who was hedging her bets on who she could make the most cash from. She flew out to Italy immediately, stayed in Perla for a few days and paid a group of local teens to ferry her out to the island the previous day with a spare rowboat to get back to the mainland in case the anonymous tip-off proved to be false. (The spare rowboat is the one in the cove.) She decided to do a bit of exploring by herself during the daytime figuring the ghosts wouldn't come out while the sun shone. Unfortunately, she poked around a bit too much and in the course of her explorations, was utterly corrupted by Hastalÿk from within. Mechanically, she has a Taint level of 10 (see p.62 for details), but appears completely normal on the outside. She will subtly lead the Investigators on in an effort to release the Grand Corruption upon the world.

The Plague Monk's physical form has been hanging above the charnel pit for years now, but he can project manifestations of himself anywhere on the large island. His goal is to lead the Investigators to places where their corruption (represented by their Taint score, see p.62) will increase, so that when they are finally led to the charnel pit, they willingly hurl themselves in.

As soon as they see him, the monk's head will rise to look at them with a series of popping cracks. This triggers a Sanity check (1/1D8). Anyone with sufficient Taint should make a POW check or feel compelled to look in the pit unless someone stops them. Anyone that steps within five feet sees a terrifying slurry of putrid flesh and fluids that swirls slowly within. Another POW check may be necessary to avoid throwing themselves into the pit (see Taint on p.62).

The third isn't as critical, but it can be very helpful for at least one of them to have The Sight (see p.60). This allows them to learn more about the true nature of what's going on, while adding to the overall mood of the story. The Investigator with The Sight could be the psychic from the group or not. It could even be interesting to have someone who has been faking psychic powers to suddenly experience real visions.

| 8 | It looks, smells, and tastes like a normal lemon. At the Keeper's discretion, the lemon could also have significant psychoactive properties that temporarily give the Investigator The Sight (see p.60). This could be useful if running one of the alternative Investigator options where none of them previously had any psychic abilities. |

VHS Recorder – The Investigators find a backpack with an mid-80s era VHS recorder and a book called Il Culto della Peste dell'Isola Malamente (see History p.16). Hyeon can rig one of his batteries to run it, and they can watch what's on the tape through the eyepiece.

xrefs.source_line: There are far too many locations within Saint Roche's Hospital to describe thoroughly, and doing so would begin to get a bit repetitive with the Keeper describing room after room that has fallen to decay and rot. The following descriptions are kept simple, with ideas for embellishment as the Spektral Krew continues their investigation. In addition to specific phenomena listed in the descriptions, the Keeper should make use of the Hospital Encounters table in the Appendix (see p.59).
xrefs.visible_text: Hospital Encounters table in the Appendix

xrefs.source_line: Just to the right of the door are the mummified remains of what appears to have been a monk judging by the rotted brown cassock clinging to the desiccated flesh. Under his left arm is clutched a leather bound book (see Iuramentum Corruptionis on p.67), and next to his right hand is an 1889 Bodeo (10.5mm) revolver. There is a clean hole in his temple. Even to someone with no forensic background, it looks to have been self-inflicted.

segments.reader_text: Infected Flesh in the The Reliquae
segments.source_text: Infected Flesh in the The Reliquae on p.67

xrefs.source_line: These undead are extremely fragile, and if attacked by a Investigator, they break apart with a single blow, falling apart like a chicken that has been pressure cooked too long. An Investigator that destroys one should make a Luck roll to avoid being covered with rotted, infected flesh (see Infected Flesh in the The Reliquae on p.67).
xrefs.visible_text: Infected Flesh in the The Reliquae

xrefs.source_line: If they shine a light in the recess, they'll see a rot-covered corpse wrapped in ragged cloth (see Plague Zombie). The flesh that hangs loosely from its bones is infested with pale worms and fungus. Its eyes are swollen milky orbs that stare with malevolence at the thief. In the depths of the shadows behind there are more sets of eyes peering from the darkness.
At this point, the Reliquae (see Appendix p.66) begin climbing out of the shelf to get the Investigators. The Keeper can decide how many pursue.

If the Keeper wants to have some sort of wrap-up, they can have the Investigators picked up by the Italian DSS and questioned, and essentially threatened into silence about what actually happened (see Expanded Ending on p.56). The Investigators shouldn't underestimate the power of the DSS to discredit them and/or make their lives difficult if they choose to not keep their mouths shut.

This option is provided should the Keeper want to have a more dramatic climax to the scenario. This naturally leads into the Expanded Ending (see p.56), which can in turn lead to an extended campaign. Once the investigators are on the surface of the island, fleeing from Hastalÿk, read the following:
If they didn't notice the previous symbol at the Weeping Bridge, then the Keeper can simply improvise using the description on page 35.

The two remaining helicopters are managing to slow The Devourer a bit, which should give the investigators a chance to get close enough to lob grenades at it. Note that if they get within 10 yards, they risk being attacked by a pseudopod and possibly being absorbed into The Devourer (see p.65).
## 1N. East Corridor – See West Corridor. This corridor connects the Admission Ward to the Staff Dormitory.

Hastalÿk Rises. Anyone present when Hastalÿk rises must make a POW check to resist a desire to join with it. Failure means that they walk as if in a trance to hurl themselves into the pit or embrace Hastalÿk. This check is modified by the amount of Taint the victim has acquired (see Taint Levels below).

8 The Stalker – In the distance, one of the cameras picks up a robed figure, like a monk. When they look with the naked eye however, they see nothing. When they look again, it's closer and walking towards them, though still nothing when they look without the camera. If they let it reach them, the area turns frigid (see Cold Spot). Either way, they must make a Sanity check (1/1D3).
The Reliquae tries to grab any living human and infect them (see Infection).

2F. Recovery Ward – See 1K.

xrefs.source_line: If anybody is stupid enough to attack armed Italian soldiers, they find themselves heavily out-gunned, outnumbered, and outmatched. The soldiers will attempt to beat them into unconsciousness (see Knock-Out Blows on p.125 in the Keeper Rulebook), though they are not above shooting the prisoners if they become too troublesome.
xrefs.visible_text: Knock-Out Blows on p.125 in the Keeper Rulebook

xrefs.source_line: In preparation for this investigation, Corrina has done some research on the island so that she's ready for whatever spirits she might encounter. Of course this also makes it easier for her to make things up on the fly. Handout #12 provides a list of facts and folklore that Corrina has learned about Isola di Malamente.

Before beginning the Prologue, the Keeper should provide Handouts #1-7 to the players, and if possible, provide them in advance and a few days apart. The first two are essentially a hype email from Marco describing the plan to stream live from the ‘haunted’ island of Isola di Malamente, and the second three are from Maya outlining the basic arrangements made for the trip. After the players have had time to read them (or listened to someone read them aloud), begin the Prologue.
The Keeper should hand the person playing Enoch Handout #11 describing his vision as they approach the island.

Exterior Description. Standing atop the rocky southern shore of Isola di Malamente's secondary island is a three story lighthouse on a crumbling concrete slab (Handout #14). The pale stone of the lighthouse is weathered, but looks as solid as it was when it was built centuries ago. An attached brick building is still standing, though its roof is drooping slightly with age. Most of the glass of the lantern deck is surprisingly intact, and you can see the silhouette of the old World War II era radio antenna within.

Description. The bridge has clearly seen better days. It's made of a simple cast iron design that was painted green at some point, but is now mostly brown with rust. Constant exposure to sun, sea, and wind have caused the paint on the metal railings to chip and fade, and the wooden planks of its surface are heavily weathered, though they seem more or less intact (Handout #28).

Description. A well-worn path leads you into a vast grove of cultivated lemon trees that feels more like a cave with the upper branches forming a dense canopy overhead. You're immediately greeted by the hazy buzz of insects, the sweet smell of citrus, and the stench of decay that catches in the back of your throat and sinuses (Handout #32).

Investigators should make a POW check at this point. Success means that they feel as if they are being watched, with a Hard success allowing them to spot what looks like a solitary figure standing in one of the second floor windows. As the Investigator stares for a moment, the figure appears to turn away into the darkness (Handout #30) triggering a Sanity check (0/1D3). Anyone else who looks afterwards sees nothing but a dark curtain moving gently in the breeze (Handout #31). This curtain is a plausible enough explanation for the figure if one wants to convince themselves that it was nothing.

The rim of the pit is marked with the stubs of several hundred candles which have fused into a mass of wax from decades of previous candles, forming a pale ring around this profane golgotha (Handout #33).

In the very center of the crypt is an ancient slab of stone that has been carved to form a low rectangular table or altar. Judging by the proportions (four feet wide by seven feet long by three feet tall), it may have been used to lay out bodies in preparation for burial, or perhaps some ancient funeral rite (Handout #34).
On a nearby stone shelf you notice an ancient book. Most of it has turned to dust and crumbling brown flakes, but there is a single fragment that seems to be intact (Handout #35).

Description. The tunnels feel like a maze cutting through the living rock of the island. You pass countless loculi or niches piled with bones and skulls. You can't help but notice the occasional reflection of trinkets and minor valuables, presumably left as final offerings to the dead that rest here. Every so often, the tunnel opens up a bit, but around the next corner, it tightens up again. The occasional side passage goes left or right... or maybe you're on the branch passage now. It's so difficult to tell (Handout #36).

Scattered throughout the catacombs are rooms for various purposes. Many are simply junctions where several tunnels meet, while others are preparation chambers. Several contain closed sarcophagi, presumably for those of higher social station. The tops are nearly impossible to open without tools, and even then requires an hour or more (Handout #37).

The bodies of the fallen, after a moment's abeyance almost in wonder at the sight before them, suddenly hurl themselves toward their blasphemous god and are absorbed into its mass. Its outer membrane rips and seethes as it grows, its massive bulk smacking against the stone ceiling. The roof cracks as more stones rain down into the chamber. Mercifully, the thing from the pit has not noticed you so far, basking in the glory of its own loathsome birth (Handout #38).

When the first bombs hit, the fireballs illuminate the entire island. Silhouetted against the flames is the writhing form of Hastalÿk, shrieking to the sky as it burns furiously. The sound of heavy cannon fire from the jets tears massive chunks from the thing as it sends out pseudopods in a vain attempt to swat the jets from the sky (Handout #39).
